candidates.statement: Effective Date: 10/22/97; 5/4/07; 5/19/2021 Page 1 of 6 POLICY AND PROCEDURES OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT CDER’s Time, Attendance, and Leave Recording Policy Table of Contents PURPOSE ................................................................ ...........1 POLICY ................................................................ ..............1 RESPONSIBILITIES ................................ ........................3 PROCEDURES ................................................................ ..4 REFERENCES ................................................................ ...5 DEFINITIONS ................................................................ ...5 EFFECTIVE DATE ................................ ...........................6 CHANGE CONTROL TABLE ................................ .........6 PURPOSE • This MAPP clarifies how CDER employees and supervisors should use the integrated time and attendance system (ITAS) to manage time and attendance information as required by the HHS Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) Remediation Project. FLSA was effective May 1, 2016.
candidates.context: • This MAPP does not change the current rules and regulations for using leave, earning and using credit and compensatory time, and earning overtime.

candidates.statement: POLICY • Leave requests, credit and compensatory time earned and used, and overtime earned must be approved by the employee’s supervisor in advance. Leave requests must be requested and approved through ITAS.
candidates.context: • This MAPP does not change the current rules and regulations for using leave, earning and using credit and compensatory time, and earning overtime. • Employees with access to ITAS must verify their timecard using the ITAS “Verify Timecard” function no later than noon the second Thursday of the pay

candidates.statement: • Employees with access to ITAS must verify their timecard using the ITAS “Verify Timecard” function no later than noon the second Thursday of the pay
candidates.context: POLICY • Leave requests, credit and compensatory time earned and used, and overtime earned must be approved by the employee’s supervisor in advance. Leave requests must be requested and approved through ITAS. Effective Date: 10/22/97; 5/4/07; 5/19/2021 Page 2 of 6 period, although timecards can be verified at any time during the second week of the pay period.

candidates.statement: • Employees must verify their timecard in ITAS before the leave approving official (i.e., the supervisor) approves the timecard.
candidates.context: Effective Date: 10/22/97; 5/4/07; 5/19/2021 Page 2 of 6 period, although timecards can be verified at any time during the second week of the pay period. • Employees requiring the timekeeper to enter approved premium hours, a change to their regularly scheduled tour hours, or leave requests in ITAS on their behalf will be required to submit a timesheet in accordance with existing office procedures. This ensures that the timekeeper has time to accurately enter the timecard data into ITAS before the employee verifies the timecard in ITAS.

candidates.statement: • Supervisors can approve the employee’s timecard in ITAS if the employee has no access to ITAS at the time the ITAS verification is due (e.g., the employee is ill, on training or foreign travel, or has technical or other issues). In such cases, the employee is required to verify the timecard electronically in ITAS immediately upon their return to duty or when their access to ITAS is restored.
candidates.context: Supervisors and timekeepers will accept a document from employees signed electronically using the PIV card as long as the document includes the employee’s printed name and the date of submission. The employee is still responsible for reporting their time and leave to the timekeeper and supervisor. If the employee cannot report their time and leave before the pay period cut off times, then they should provide this information immediately upon their return so any deviations in time or leave can be entered as supplements in the following pay period.

candidates.context: • Supervisors can approve the employee’s timecard in ITAS if the employee has no access to ITAS at the time the ITAS verification is due (e.g., the employee is ill, on training or foreign travel, or has technical or other issues). In such cases, the employee is required to verify the timecard electronically in ITAS immediately upon their return to duty or when their access to ITAS is restored. • Timekeepers must have timecards ready for supervisor approval by 3:00 p.m. All timecards must be approved by supervisors by COB the second Thursday of the pay period.

candidates.statement: • Timekeepers must have timecards ready for supervisor approval by 3:00 p.m. All timecards must be approved by supervisors by COB the second Thursday of the pay period.

If the employee cannot report their time and leave before the pay period cut off times, then they should provide this information immediately upon their return so any deviations in time or leave can be entered as supplements in the following pay period. • If an employee’s hours have changed after the supervisor has approved the timecard in ITAS, a supplement is required.

candidates.statement: Effective Date: 10/22/97; 5/4/07; 5/19/2021 Page 3 of 6 Timekeepers are required to process supplements in ITAS. The employee must submit a revised timesheet to the timekeeper identifying the change in hours worked. Any supplement created by the timekeeper will be verified by the employee during the pay period in which the supplement was created.
candidates.context: • If an employee’s hours have changed after the supervisor has approved the timecard in ITAS, a supplement is required. • Timekeepers will work with supervisors to establish and communicate their processing timelines. Established timelines must ensure that the CDER deadline of COB Thursday the second week of the pay period is met.

candidates.statement: RESPONSIBILITIES Employees must: • Request leave in advance in ITAS when possible.
candidates.context: • The timekeeper will maintain all time and attendance documents electronically in the employee’s electronic timekeeping file for 3 years plus the current year. • Request approval before working premium hours. • Provide a timesheet to the timekeeper by specified time required by office if unusual leave, premium hours, or change in tour needs to be recorded by the timekeeper.

candidates.statement: Timekeepers must: • Work with the supervisor(s) to establish and communicate office processing times.
candidates.context: Effective Date: 10/22/97; 5/4/07; 5/19/2021 Page 4 of 6 • Work with the timekeeper to establish and communicate office processing times. • Enter premium hours, change in tour hours, and unusual leave in ITAS on the employee’s behalf – notify the employee to verify the timecard.

candidates.statement: ITAS Administrative Officer must: • At the end of each leave year, review the timekeeping files and move the electronic timekeeping records to their office’s appropriate timekeeping record folder in ECMS FDA-RM to align with FDA-9313a Time and Attendance Records requirements.
candidates.context: • Maintain all records (e.g., Administrative Time and Leave Record Form HHS- 564, LES) in employee’s electronic timekeeping file for 3 years plus the current year. • Following the validation of the transfer of all records to ECMS FDA-RM, delete files from the shared drive.

FDA Staff Manual Guide 1430.5, Volume 11 – Delegations of Authority – Authority to Approve Overtime (effective 12/18/15) DEFINITIONS Premium Hours are hours worked in addition to the basic work requirement that must be entered into ITAS by the timekeeper that include overtime, compensatory time, credit hours, compensatory time for travel, and religious compensatory time.
candidates.context: Timecard is the form in ITAS that the employee, or timekeeper, uses to report and verify all work hours.

candidates.statement: Unusual Leave are leave categories that must be entered into ITAS by the timekeeper, which include religious compensatory time, VLTP, advanced annual, and advanced sick leave.
candidates.context: Timesheet is the CDER Timesheet that the employee submits to the timekeeper when ITAS is not available or unusual leave, premium hours, or a change in hours of tour are requested.
